headline: Mandi-Manali stretch may reopen today
content: Shimla: The stretch of Mandi-Manali highway blocked between Mandi and Pandoh at 6 Miles is likely to be reopened by Wednesday, while the road beyond Pandoh continues to remains blocked near Aut. The Kullu-Mandi stretch is through up to Pandoh and the traffic is further diverted via Gohar-Chailchowk-Sundernagar route. After the restoration of road connectivity between Manali and Kullu, 4,500 vehicles have moved out of the tourist town. The road from Pandoh to Gohar-Chailchowk-Baggi-Sundernagar is open for light motor vehicles only. The traffic from Kullu to Mandi will be diverted from Pandoh to Gohar-Chailchowk-Baggi-Sundernagar after opening of one tunnel and national highway at Aut. The road to Kullu via Kataula-Kamand is through for one-way traffic at many places for light motor vehicles only. The Pathankot-Mandi highway between Mandi and Jogindernagar is through for all types of vehicular traffic, so is the highway between Mandi and Bilaspur. The road connectivity between Kullu and Manali that was disrupted at multiple points due to overflowing Beas river has been restored. Only light motor vehicles are allowed to ply on the left bank via Archhandi, Raison, from where they have to move to the right bank. At least 4,500 vehicles have moved safely out of Manali of which, 400 had crossed Kullu by 7pm, police officials said. According to the information provided by the police, Shimla-Chandigarh national highway is also through, but with bottlenecks at certain places. In the state, heavy rainfall coupled with flashfloods have also disrupted the water and electricity supply. Total 1,239 roads, including three national highways, are still blocked across the state, while 2,577 distribution transformers and 1,418 water supply schemes have been disrupted. As per the state emergency operations centre, the public works department has suffered a loss of Rs 616 crore, Jal Shakti department Rs 350.5 crore, horticulture department Rs 70.36 crore, urban development department Rs 3.15 crore and state electricity board Rs 92 lakh.
